Heard learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the appellants and Sri Kolluri Arjun Chowdary, learned counsel appearing for the respondents.
The Special Deputy Collector La vs Ch Subbamma on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27833035/

entities.text: Special Deputy Collector La vs Ch Subbamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 2. Respondents 1 to 129 were the owners of various extents of land in Jonnavaram Village, Atloor Mandal.
These lands had been acquired under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the Act') for submergence under Somasila Project.
3. Draft Notification under Section 4(1) of the Act was published on 29.09.1999 and an award in relation to these lands was passed on 28.03.2005.
This award is said to be a consent award wherein the private respondents are said to have accepted the amounts shown under the consent award.

4. Thereafter, the private respondents again approached the respondent authorities for payment of 12% additional market value on the award amount from the date of taking possession till the date of notification issued from 26.09.1999 to 06.12.2004.

It was the contention of the private respondents that the respondent authorities had taken advance possession of the land of the private HCJ &
RRR,J respondents on 24.09.1998, even before the notifications had been issued under the Act and as such they are entitled to interest at the rate of 12% per annum for the period between the date of taking possession and passing of the award.
This request was rejected by the respondent authorities on the ground that no advance possession of the land had been taken.
Due to this rejection, the private respondents had approached this Court by way of W.P.No.6373 of 2022.

This writ petition was allowed by a learned Single Judge of this Court by an order dated 21.02.2023.
5.

The learned Single Judge, on the basis of the proceedings, dated 24.09.1998, showing handing over of physical possession of the affected lands by the Deputy Collector, to the Deputy Executive Engineer, Atmakur, had held that possession had been handed over on 24.09.1998 even before the proceedings under the Act commencing with the draft notification under Section 4(1) had been initiated.
Aggrieved by this order, the present writ appeal has been filed.
6. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition assails the order of the learned Single Judge on two grounds.

Firstly, she contends that no advance possession had been taken over and the finding of the learned Single Judge stating that HCJ & RRR,J advance possession is reflected by the proceedings dated 24.09.1998 is incorrect.
She contends that, as the said proceedings are not available in the record of the respondents, they cannot be treated as genuine proceedings.

Secondly,
the award dated 28.03.2005 is a consent award and no additional payments can be given until the said consent award has been set aside.

She relies upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the State of Karnataka and Anr., vs. Sangappa Dyavappa Biradar & Ors.,1 and Singana Subba Reddy vs. Principal Secretary, Irrigation Department, State of A.P., in W.P.No.27235 and 11881 of 2018 dated 18.01.2022, passed by this Hon'ble Court.

sentences.text: 7. Sri Kolluru Arjun Chowdary, learned counsel appearing for the respondents would rely upon the judgments in Government of A.P. vs. The L.A.O. & M.R.O. Hanamkonda & Ors.,2; and Chandra Bansi Singh and Ors., vs. State of Bihar and Ors.,3 and an unreported judgment of a Division Bench of the erstwhile High Court for the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh in W.A.No.187 of 2010 dated 01.11.2017.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

The learned counsel relying upon the above judgments would contend that the possession of the land was not taken under the provisions of the Land Acquisition AIR 2005 SC 2204 = (2005) 4 SCC 264 1993 (2) APLJ 402 (HC) (1984) 4 SCC 316 HCJ & RRR,J Act, 1894 and as such any consent award accepted by the private respondents, would only be in The Special Deputy Collector La vs Ch Subbamma on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27833035/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: relation to the compensation payable under the Act while the compensation now sought by the private respondents is on account of the advance possession being taken without any reference to the provisions of the Act.

Consideration of the Court:
8. On the question of whether advance possession has been taken on 24.09.1998, the same does not require any elaborate enquiry as the proceedings dated 24.09.1998 placed before this Court demonstrates that the acquisition authorities had handed over possession of the said lands to the Irrigation Department on 24.09.1998.

The contention of the learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition that the said proceedings are not genuine as such the proceedings are not available in the records of the respondent authorities, cannot be accepted.
Mere non availability of the documents in the records of the authorities cannot be a ground to dismiss documents produced by the other side.
9. State of Karnataka and Anr., vs. Sangappa Dyavappa Biradar & Ors., was a case where the land losers had accepted a consent award and had thereafter sought reference under Section 18 of the Act.

entities.text: State of Karnataka and Anr., vs. Sangappa Dyavappa Biradar & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in view of the language of HCJ & RRR,J section 18 of the land Acquisition Act 1894, held that a reference is maintainable only if the award has not been accepted.

As the land losers had accepted the award, without any demur, the Hon'ble Supreme court had declared that the land losers, in that case, were estopped and precluded from maintaining an application for reference in terms of Section 18 of the Act.

10. Singana Subba Reddy vs. Principal Secretary, Irrigation Department, State of A.P., in W.P.No.27235 and 11881 of 2018 dated 18.01.2022, passed by this Hon'ble Court, was a case where compensation was sought to be enhanced on the ground that proper market value had not been taken into account.

entities.text: Singana Subba Reddy vs. Principal Secretary, Irrigation Department, State of A.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A learned Single judge of this Court, had held that such claims fall squarely within the ambit of a reference under section 18 of the land Acquisition Act, 1894 and such claims are not maintainable after the award had been accepted by the land losers.
11. In Chandra Bansi Singh vs. State of Bihar, possession of the land had been taken a long time after the notification under section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act had been issued.

entities.text: Chandra Bansi Singh vs. State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The affected persons claimed that, in view of the delay, the prices of land had appreciated substantially and compensation should be paid on the value of the land prevailing on the date of taking possession.

The HCJ &
RRR,J Hon'ble Supreme Court, after rejecting this plea, on the facts of that case, had held as follows:
16. On an analysis of the various steps taken by the parties and others in the taking of possession, there is undoubtedly a delay of about 1 years and for the purpose of calculation and convenience when rounded off, the delay may be taken to be of two years.

So far as this delay is concerned, the appellants have undoubtedly a case for payment of some additional compensation in equity though not under law and as this Court is not only a Court of law but a Court of equity as well, it will be impossible for us to deny this relief to the appellants.

After taking into consideration the various shades and aspects of the case we are clearly of the opinion that apart from compensation which may be awarded by the Collector or enhanced by the Judge or a The Special Deputy Collector La vs Ch Subbamma on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27833035/
3

entities.text: Special Deputy Collector La vs Ch Subbamma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: higher Court, the appellants should get an equitable compensation in the form of interest calculated at the rate of 7 per cent per annum for two years on the value of land owned by each land-owner.
This equitable compensation has been awarded in the special facts of this case and will not be the subject-matter of appeal, if any, under the Act on the amount of compensation.

12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court had differentiated between compensation payable under the Act and compensation that can be awarded in such situations, even if such compensation does not arise under the land Acquisition Act.
The Hon'ble Supreme court had also awarded compensation which was not based on the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.

Following this judgement a division bench of the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh, in HCJ & RRR,J Chilukuri Rama Rao vs.
Government of Andhra Pradesh4, while dealing with a consent award, had directed payment of interest, on account of delayed payment of compensation.

entities.text:
HCJ & RRR,J Chilukuri Rama Rao vs.
Government of Andhra Pradesh4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. A single judge of the erstwhile high Court of Andhra Pradesh in Government of Andhra Pradesh vs. Land Acquisition Officer And Mandal Revenue Officer, Hanamkonda, had held that the land losers were entitled to equitable compensation, for the period, when possession of land is taken prior to issuance of necessary notification under the Land Acquisition Act and the date of award.

entities.text: Government of Andhra Pradesh vs. Land Acquisition Officer And Mandal Revenue Officer, Hanamkonda
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A division bench of the Hon'ble High Court at Hyderabad for the states of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, in Writ Appeal No.187 of 2010, after referring to these judgements and the Judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Assistant Commissioner, Gadag Sub Division vs. Mathapathi Basavannewwa and Ors.,5 had held that award of such compensation in cases , where advance possession has been taken is permissible.

entities.text: Assistant Commissioner, Gadag Sub Division vs. Mathapathi Basavannewwa and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The view taken by the Court, in this regard, is that advance possession of the land, taken by the authorities, would not be a proceeding under the Act and as such compensation can be awarded de hors the Act, in relation to an action which is not under the Land Acquisition Act.

In view of this vital difference in the nature of the compensation sought by the private respondents, it cannot be said that the direction of the learned Single Judge for payment of compensation for the relevant period is not in accordance with law.
15. Accordingly, this writ appeal is dismissed.
However, this Court does not deem the interest at the rate of 12 % per annum to be a reasonable compensation.
Keeping in view the historical rates of interest being offered by banks, during the relevant period, this court is of the opinion that interest at the rate of 7% per annum would be fair compensation.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

DHIRAJ SINGH THAKUR, CJ R. RAGHUNANDAN RAO, J JS.
HCJ & RRR,J HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE DHIRAJ SINGH THAKUR, CHIEF JUSTICE & HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE R. RAGHUNANDAN RAO (per Hon'ble Sri Justice R.Raghunandan Rao) 12th March,
